data.one_liner: Dart server and client implementation of Socket.io for real‑time bidirectional communication.
data.what_it_does: Provides a Server class to host a Socket.io server and a client library to connect from Dart. Supports namespaces, rooms, and both polling and WebSocket transports, mirroring the JavaScript Socket.io API.
use_when: You need real‑time, event‑driven communication between Dart/Flutter apps and a backend that already uses Socket.io
You want built‑in support for namespaces and rooms without writing low‑level WebSocket handling
avoid_when: A simple HTTP/REST request is sufficient
You need the latest Socket.io v3+ features that this package (v2) may not support
strengths: Namespace and room abstractions are provided out of the box
Works on all major platforms (mobile, desktop, server)
weaknesses: Implements only Socket.io v2.0.1, may lag behind newer server versions
Less active community compared to raw WebSocket packages

alternatives.name: web_socket_channel
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides a lightweight, low‑level WebSocket client/server without Socket.io overhead, suitable for simple real‑time needs

alternatives.name: shelf_web_socket
alternatives.why_pick_it: Allows building WebSocket endpoints on the server side using the Shelf ecosystem
